text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
-U.S. investment fund Tiger says it believes that the proposed merger between Norway's largest insurer Storebrand and commercial bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse will come about.
-Kvaerner expects stable demand for shipbuilding because the world fleet is ageing and because of increasing safety demands.

-Fokus Bank probably bought 2.9 million shares in Storebrand on Thursday. Lawyers say however that Fokus may have bought the shares too late to be allowed to vote on the proposed merger between Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse at Storebrand's general assembly on June 26.
-The Norwegian stock exchange has no immediate plans to join a joint share-trading system agreed by the neighbouring Swedish and Danish bourses.

-The opposition Christian People's Party is gaining support in an opinion poll released three months before Norway's parliamentary election in September. The ruling minority Labour government is losing ground.
-Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner is drawing up plans for the construction of the world's first gas-production ship.

-The board of Norwegian food and beverage conglomerate Orkla has asked CEO Jens Heyerdahl to decide whether or not to support the proposed merger between Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse. Orkla holds 13.55 percent of share capital in Storebrand.
-Coopers & Lybrand is aiming at becoming Norway's largest lawyer firm by the year 2000.
